body.content: Speculative mechanism: The panel's advantage might be a COMPOSITION effect (wisdom of crowds) that is independent of the checklist. A corrupted-checklist control (Candidate 5) tests this. If the corrupted-checklist panel still outperforms the expert, the checklist is epiphenomenal. But what if the checklist's role is not to supply rules but to STRUCTURE panel deliberation (e.g., ensure each criterion is discussed)? Then a corrupted checklist might still help by structuring discussion, even with wrong rules. This would be a genuine but non-epistemic checklist contribution.
body.possible_next_move: Design a control that preserves deliberation structure but corrupts rule content, vs. one that removes structure entirely.
body.why_keep_this: Identifies a confound: checklist-as-procedure vs. checklist-as-content.
